- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model frequently underestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–3% per 3-day horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30), model tends to overestimate future prices — apply a 2–5% downward bias for 5–10 day horizon.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven mean reversion in 10+ day horizons — apply a 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment has been positive for 5+ days.
- If sentiment is volatile or erratic (e.g., alternating +/–0.30), model overfits short-term noise — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ values before applying correction.
